title: H-Index II
summary: Given an array of integers citations sorted in non-descending order, find the maximum value of h such that the researcher has at least h papers each cited at least h times.
statement: Given an array of integers citations sorted in non-descending order, find the maximum value of h such that the researcher has at least h papers each cited at least h times. The algorithm must run in logarithmic time.
constraints: citations contains 1–100000 integers from 0 through 1000 in nondecreasing order.
Return the largest h for which at least h papers have at least h citations. Use logarithmic time.
hints: At index i, exactly n-i papers have citations at least citations[i].
Search for the first index where citations[i]≥n-i; feasibility stays true to its right.
Use a half-open [left,right) binary search. Move right to mid when feasible, otherwise move left past mid.
After convergence, n-left is the maximum feasible suffix length; if no index works, left=n and the answer is zero.
editorial: Sorted citations make the predicate citations[i]≥n-i monotone: once a suffix has enough citations per paper, every later shorter suffix also does. Binary search finds the first feasible index, and its suffix length is the h-index. The independent oracle ignores sortedness and directly checks every candidate against all citations.

tests.explanation: At index 2, three papers remain and citation 3 reaches that count; no earlier feasible index gives a larger h.
No paper has even one citation, so the h-index is 0.
